books.title: Narrative of the Life of Frederick Douglass
books.author: Frederick Douglass
books.desc: Born into slavery in Maryland, Frederick Douglass tells how he learned to read, resisted a brutal overseer and won his freedom.
about: Douglass describes his birth into slavery in Talbot County, Maryland, separated from his mother as an infant and never knowing his exact age. He recounts the cruelty he witnessed on Colonel Lloyd's plantation, his years in Baltimore, where his mistress began to teach him the alphabet until her husband forbade it, and how he went on teaching himself in secret. Hired out to Edward Covey, a farmer notorious for breaking the will of enslaved people, he finally fights back. The book ends with his escape to the North and his new life in New Bedford, Massachusetts.

Written in a clear and powerful style, the Narrative is both a personal testimony and an argument against slavery, showing how it degrades both the enslaved and the enslavers and exposing the hypocrisy of slaveholding Christianity. Douglass deliberately gives no details of his escape in order to protect those who might still use the same route.

The Narrative was published in Boston in 1845 by the Anti-Slavery Office, with a preface by William Lloyd Garrison and a letter by Wendell Phillips. It sold some 5,000 copies in its first four months and became the best-known of the American slave narratives.
books.author_short: American abolitionist, writer and statesman (1818–1895), who escaped slavery and wrote three autobiographies.
author_long: Frederick Douglass was born into slavery in Talbot County, Maryland, probably in 1818, as Frederick Augustus Washington Bailey. In September 1838 he escaped to the North. He became a celebrated speaker and writer against slavery, founded the newspaper The North Star, and took part in the first women's rights convention at Seneca Falls in 1848. From 1889 to 1891 he was United States minister to Haiti. He died on 20 February 1895.
His three autobiographies are Narrative of the Life of Frederick Douglass, an American Slave (1845), My Bondage and My Freedom (1855) and Life and Times of Frederick Douglass (1881).

books.title: The Narrative of Arthur Gordon Pym of Nantucket
books.author: Edgar Allan Poe
books.desc: A young man stows away on a whaling ship and is drawn into mutiny, shipwreck, starvation and a strange voyage towards the South Pole.
about: Arthur Gordon Pym of Nantucket, eager for adventure, is smuggled aboard the whaling brig Grampus by his friend Augustus Barnard, whose father is its captain, and hidden in the hold with his dog Tiger. A bloody mutiny breaks out, and Pym, Augustus and the sailor Dirk Peters fight to survive, then drift on the wreck, suffering terribly from hunger and thirst. Rescued by the British schooner Jane Guy, Pym sails into the Antarctic seas, towards an unknown island called Tsalal.

Poe's only completed novel mixes the sea adventure, the horror tale and the false travel narrative, presented as a true account. Its depiction of the black-skinned islanders of Tsalal and of the "half-breed" Dirk Peters reflects the racial attitudes of its time.
The novel was published by Harper & Brothers in July 1838, after a few opening instalments had appeared in the Southern Literary Messenger.
books.author_short: American writer and critic (1809–1849), master of the tale of terror, credited with inventing the detective story.
author_long: Edgar Allan Poe was born in Boston on 19 January 1809. His father left the family and his mother, an actress, died when he was two. He was taken into the Richmond home of John and Frances Allan, whose surname he later used as his middle name. He worked as an editor and critic for several magazines, and died in Baltimore on 7 October 1849, aged 40.

His poem "The Raven" (1845) made him famous. He wrote many tales of mystery and horror, such as "The Fall of the House of Usher", and with "The Murders in the Rue Morgue" is credited with inventing detective fiction. The Narrative of Arthur Gordon Pym (1838) is his only completed novel.

books.title: The Fall of the House of Usher
books.author: Edgar Allan Poe
books.desc: Summoned by an old friend, a visitor arrives at a gloomy mansion where the last of the Usher family is slowly sinking into madness.
about: One dark autumn day, the narrator arrives at the melancholy House of Usher in answer to a letter from his boyhood friend Roderick Usher, who suffers from a nervous illness and an extreme sensitivity of the senses. Roderick's twin sister, Madeline, is wasting away from a mysterious disease. The narrator tries to distract his friend with reading, painting and music, but the atmosphere of the decaying house weighs on them all.
Poe's tale is a classic of Gothic fiction, in which the decaying house mirrors the minds and the fate of the family that lives in it. It explores fear, madness, isolation and the bond between twins.

"The Fall of the House of Usher" was first published in September 1839 in Burton's Gentleman's Magazine and, slightly revised, in Poe's collection Tales of the Grotesque and Arabesque (1840). It includes the poem "The Haunted Palace", which Poe had published separately earlier in 1839.

books.title: The Happy Prince and Other Tales
books.author: Oscar Wilde
books.desc: Five fairy tales, from a golden statue who gives away his riches to a nightingale who sacrifices herself for love.
about: High above a city stands the statue of the Happy Prince, covered in gold leaf and jewels. From there he sees the misery of the poor, and he asks a little Swallow, who has stayed behind on his journey to Egypt, to carry his treasures to them. The collection also contains "The Nightingale and the Rose", "The Selfish Giant", "The Devoted Friend" and "The Remarkable Rocket".
Written in the form of fairy tales for children, Wilde's stories mix wit and tenderness, and speak of generosity, sacrifice, selfishness and vanity, often with a melancholy ending.
The Happy Prince and Other Tales was published in London by David Nutt in May 1888, with illustrations by Walter Crane and Jacomb Hood.

books.title: Mrs. Warren's Profession
books.author: George Bernard Shaw
books.desc: A brilliant young Cambridge graduate discovers how her mother made the fortune that paid for her education.
about: Vivie Warren, a clever and independent young woman who has just done brilliantly in mathematics at Cambridge, is spending time in a cottage in Surrey when her mother, whom she barely knows, arrives with her friends, the artistic Mr Praed and the coarse Sir George Crofts. Vivie is also courted by Frank Gardner, the idle son of the local clergyman. Questioning her mother, she discovers the source of the money that has supported her all her life.

Shaw's play attacks the hypocrisy of a society that condemns prostitution while leaving poor women few other means of escaping poverty, and that profits from it in respectable ways. It also portrays a new kind of independent, working woman in Vivie.

Shaw completed the play in 1893, but the Lord Chamberlain refused to license it for public performance. It was published in Plays Unpleasant in 1898 and first performed privately by the Stage Society in London on 5 January 1902. This edition includes the author's apology of 1902.
